title: DNA extraction, PCR amplification, and sequencing of Colletotrichum species
author: Le Dinh Thao
materials: Total genomic DNA from the herbarium specimen was extracted using the DNeasy Plant Mini Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany) with a modification.
The tube was incubated overnight at 65 °C.

PCR products were purified using the QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany) and checked by gel electrophoresis before being sent to Macrogen (Seoul, South Korea) for sequencing. All primers used for PCR amplification were also used for sequencing.

steps.title: Collect symptomatic tissue
steps.instruction: Using a sterile scalpel under a SteREO Discovery.V12 microscope, excise approximately 5 mg of symptomatic tissue bearing Colletotrichum conidiomata from the specimen.

steps.title: Transfer tissue to bead tube
steps.instruction: Place the collected tissue into a 2‑mL Lysing Matrix E tube (MP Biomedicals) that contains 0.1 mm silica spheres, 1.4 mm ceramic spheres, and one 4 mm glass bead.

steps.title: Lyse tissue with buffer and RNase
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL AP1 buffer (from the kit) and 4 µL RNase to the tube, then disrupt the tissue using a FastPrep‑24™ instrument (MP Biomedicals).

steps.title: Purify DNA per kit protocol
steps.instruction: Carry out the subsequent DNA‑extraction steps exactly as described in the kit’s manufacturer instructions.

steps.title: Set up PCR reactions
steps.instruction: Prepare PCR mixtures to a final volume of 25 µL for each target gene, adding the appropriate primer pairs and DNA template.

substeps.instruction: Add ITS2 primers: forward ITSCF1 (5′‑GTAATGTGAATTGCAGAATTCAGTG‑3′) and reverse ITS4.
Add GAPDH primers: GDF1/GDR1 (amplifies a 200‑bp intron).
Adjust the mixture with water and PCR master mix to reach a total volume of 25 µL.

steps.title: Run PCR thermal cycle
steps.instruction: Thermal‑cycle the reactions with an initial denaturation at 94 °C for 5 min; then 35 cycles of 94 °C for 30 s, 58 °C for 30 s, and 72 °C for 1 min; finish with a final extension at 72 °C for 5 min.
